instructions.title: Warm the Broth
instructions.description: Pour the vegetable broth into a saucepan and keep it on a low simmer next to your main cooking pot. Cold broth shocks the rice and stops the cooking process, preventing the creamy texture from developing.

instructions.title: Sauté the Mushrooms
instructions.description: In your heavy-bottomed pot, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until browned and their liquid has evaporated (about 5-8 minutes). Season with a pinch of salt. Remove mushrooms from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Aromatics and Toasting
instructions.description: Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil to the pot. Add shallots and cook until softened (2-3 minutes). Add garlic and thyme, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the Arborio rice. Toast the rice, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until the edges are translucent.

instructions.title: Deglaze
instructions.description: Pour in the white wine. Stir constantly until the wine is fully absorbed by the rice.

instructions.title: The Risotto Method
instructions.description: Begin adding the warm broth, one ladle (about 0.5 cup) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until the liquid is almost completely absorbed before adding the next ladle. Repeat this process for about 20-25 minutes. The rice is done when it is tender but still has a slight bite (al dente).

instructions.title: The Finish (Mantecatura)
instructions.description: Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the cooked mushrooms, vegan butter, and nutritional yeast. Vigorously stir the mixture for 30 seconds to emulsify the fats with the starch. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

phases.action: Chop vegetables, slice mushrooms, warm broth
Brown mushrooms, sweat shallots, toast rice
Add broth gradually, stir frequently to release starch
Remove from heat, beat in fat (mantecatura) for creaminess

props.alt: A bowl of creamy vegan mushroom risotto, garnished with fresh parsley

props.text: This recipe creates a rich, velvety risotto for 4 people without using dairy. The key to the creamy texture lies in the high starch content of Arborio rice and the agitation process (stirring), which releases that starch into the broth. We will use a mix of mushrooms for depth of flavor and finish with a "mantecatura" technique using vegan fat to emulsify the sauce.

This recipe assumes you have a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. You can substitute extra vegetable broth mixed with a teaspoon of lemon juice or white wine vinegar for the dry white wine if you prefer an alcohol-free version. We assume the use of store-bought low-sodium vegetable broth.

props.alt: Risotto being cooked in a pot

games.title: Codenames
games.description: The group splits into two teams, Red and Blue. Each team has a Spymaster who provides one-word clues linked to multiple cards on the table. The goal is for teammates to guess the correct words based on the clue without picking the opposing team's words or the instant-loss Assassin card. It encourages clever thinking and group discussion.

games.title: Just One
games.description: This is a fully cooperative game where everyone wins or loses together. One player is the guesser, and the other five write one-word clues to help them guess a specific word. The catch is that if any two players write the exact same clue, those clues are erased and the guesser never sees them. It forces players to be creative rather than obvious.

games.title: Deception: Murder in Hong Kong
games.description: One player is secretly the Murderer, and another is the Forensic Scientist who knows the solution but can only communicate by placing markers on scene tiles (like Cause of Death: Suffocation). The remaining players are investigators trying to interpret these vague clues to identify the murderer and the weapon used. It is less aggressive than other lying games because the focus is on the evidence.

games.title: The Resistance
games.description: Players are members of a resistance group trying to overthrow a government, but spies have infiltrated the ranks. In each round, a leader proposes a team to go on a mission. Everyone votes to approve the team. If the mission goes ahead, players on the team secretly choose to Support or Sabotage the mission. The goal is to deduce who the saboteurs are based on voting patterns and mission results.

props.text: These recommendations assume the group has little to no prior experience with modern hobby board games. The selections focus on high interaction, minimal downtime between turns, and rules that can be taught in under 5 minutes. The games selected bridge the gap between casual conversation and structured play, ensuring the 60-minute time limit is respected even with teaching time included.

itinerary.title: Arashiyama Nature & Wildlife
itinerary.description: Start at JR Saga-Arashiyama Station. Walk 15 minutes to the Monkey Park entrance; the climb is an easy 20-minute trail with monkeys at the summit. Afterward, cross the Togetsukyo Bridge to the Bamboo Grove.

itinerary.title: Iconic Gates & Views
itinerary.description: Morning at Fushimi Inari (JR Inari Station is immediately adjacent). The lower loop hike is gentle and features thousands of gates. Afternoon: Take a taxi to Kiyomizu-dera to avoid the steep approach walk.

itinerary.title: Gold Pavilion & Trains
itinerary.description: Morning: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion). Access via taxi or direct bus to minimize walking. Afternoon: Kyoto Railway Museum (adjacent to Umekoji-Kyotonishi Station). Interactive and ideal for ages 8-10.

dining.details: "Omen" near Ginkaku-ji or Arashiyama offers dipping noodles that are fun for kids.

dining.name: Okonomiyaki
dining.details: Savory pancakes where you can watch the food being cooked on a hotplate. "Donguri" is a family-friendly chain.

dining.name: Department Store Basements (Depachika)

props.text: Visiting Kyoto in early April places you in the peak of spring season. While cherry blossoms (sakura) may be starting to flutter down by April 5-7, the city will be vibrant and busy. This itinerary balances the crowds by mixing popular historical sites with ample outdoor space for children. The schedule prioritizes locations with direct transit access or short taxi rides to strictly limit transit-to-destination walking to under 30 minutes.
To accommodate children ages 8 and 10 and the walking constraints, this plan utilizes a "hub" approach where you visit one major area in the morning and one in the afternoon.

Use JR lines and the subway where possible to avoid traffic. For Kiyomizu-dera, a taxi is recommended from the nearest station (Kyoto Station or Kiyomizu-Gojo) to the top of the hill to save energy for the actual temple grounds.
The hikes selected (Monkey Park and Fushimi Inari) are the activities themselves, not transit walks. Both have rest stops and safe paths.
Early April averages 10-20 degrees Celsius (50-68 F). Rain is possible, so indoor backups like the Railway Museum are included.
Families in Kyoto often prefer casual dining where noise levels are acceptable and menus are visual.

props.text: January is widely considered the peak travel season for both cities, but for very different reasons. Bangkok experiences its "cool" season, which is dry and sunny but still hot by global standards. Hanoi experiences a true winter, which is significantly cooler and often overcast with mist. For a walking tour, Hanoi offers much more comfortable temperatures, while Bangkok guarantees brighter photography conditions at the cost of heat exhaustion risks.

The following comparison relies on historical climate averages collected over the last 30 years. January weather patterns in Southeast Asia are generally stable, but short-term fluctuations can occur. "Rainfall probability" here refers to the likelihood of measurable precipitation days, though intensity varies (Bangkok rain is rare/short; Hanoi rain is often a persistent light drizzle).

You prioritize physical comfort and want to explore the Old Quarter for hours without sweating. The cooler temperatures (similar to a mild European autumn) make it ideal for long treks, though photographs may look gloomy due to the common "milk fog."

You want vibrant blue skies for photography and don't mind the heat. Walking tours here are best done early morning (6:00 AM - 10:00 AM) or late evening. Mid-day walking is strenuous due to the blazing sun.
